Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Russian Aerospace Forces Yury Grekhov has been arrested in Moscow, Russian media report. 

For the past five years, Grekhov was responsible for armaments of the Russian Aerospace Forces.

The arrest ruling was issued on November 25 by the 235th Garrison Military Court at the request of the Main Military Investigation Directorate of the Investigative Committee of Russia.

By unofficial reports, the arrest is due to large-scale bribery, same as ex-deputy defense minister Tsalikov who was recently sentenced to 10 years in prison.

From 2018 to 2021, Grekhov commanded the Air and Missile Defense Forces of the Russian Aerospace Forces.

This week, Putin demanded more protection for Russian oil refineries and energy infrastructure from Ukrainian drone attacks. It is not uncommon in Russia for corruption cases to open up days after failures of a specific military branch are mentioned by the Kremlin.

Since 2022, Yury Grekhov has been under sanctions from the EU, Switzerland, Japan, and New Zealand. The Council of the EU holds him responsible for the actions of the Russian Aerospace Forces in Ukraine, as he was directly in charge of supplying the troops with armaments.

Grekhov's arrest amid large-scale and productive Ukrainian strikes on Russian air defense systems and aviation equipment points to the continuation of "purges" within Russia's security bloc and the search for scapegoats for operational failures.

Grekhov's arrest fits into a wave of high-profile detentions of Russian generals (notably in the cases of Timur Ivanov, Yury Kuznetsov, and Vadim Shamarin).

The Kremlin uses anti-corruption charges as a tool to punish failures on the front lines, heavy aviation losses, and the vulnerability of Russian air defenses to Ukrainian drones and missiles, as well as a weapon in infighting among Kremlin elites. Such arrests demonstrate a lack of unity within Russia's military-political leadership and the Kremlin's distrust of its own top brass.

🇺🇸 Elon has announced an $18.35 billion pledge in SpaceX shares to American children.

Each of America's roughly 72 million children would receive 2 shares, one from SpaceX and another from Elon's personal holdings, worth around $255 combined at current prices.

SpaceX is expected to distribute its shares in December, while Elon's personal contribution is scheduled for June 2027.

In order to claim the initial shares, parents must activate their children's Trump Accounts, which are tax-advantaged investment accounts for minors.
